definitions.explanation: The act of accompanying someone to their point of departure.
Putting off a decision or action.
In baseball, not swinging at a pitch.

notes:
{見送|みおく}り is the noun form of ⟦{見送|みおく}る→見送る：04240_miokuru⟧. It has three distinct meanings: seeing someone off, postponement, and letting a pitch pass in baseball.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見送|みおく}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go see someone off
- {見送|みおく}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to see someone off
- {見送|みおく}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to be shelved/postponed
- {見送|みおく}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to decide to pass on/shelve
- {見送|みおく}り⟦{三振|さんしん}→三振：08588_sanshin⟧: called strikeout (baseball)

SENSE DISTINCTION:
- Sense 1 (farewell): accompanying someone to the station, airport, etc.
- Sense 2 (postponement): deciding not to proceed with something
- Sense 3 (baseball): not swinging at a pitch

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{見送|みおく}る→見送る：04240_miokuru⟧: to see off; to postpone; to let pass (verb form)
